\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कक्षा} (kakṣā)}{कक्षा (kakṣā)}]{\sk{कक्षा} (kakṣā) — a class, a classroom}

\label{lesson:SA-C168-kaksa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a she-goat, then the Sanskrit for a mare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कक्षा}}
\textbf{\sk{कक्षा}} — \emph{kakṣā} — \textquotedblleft{}a class, a classroom\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kakṣā} is built on \emph{kakṣa} \textquotedblleft{}hiding place, armpit\textquotedblright{}, as its feminine; MW gives it as \textquotedblleft{}a walled enclosure, a private room\textquotedblright{}. Using it for a school class and its room is modern.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अध्यायः} (adhyāyaḥ)}{अध्यायः (adhyāyaḥ)}]{\sk{अध्यायः} (adhyāyaḥ) — a chapter}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a mare, then the Sanskrit for a class.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अध्यायः}}
\textbf{\sk{अध्यायः}} — \emph{adhyāyaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a chapter\textquotedblright{}.

\emph{adhyāya} comes from \emph{adhi-√i} \textquotedblleft{}go over, study\textquotedblright{}, the root √i \textquotedblleft{}go\textquotedblright{} with \emph{adhi} \textquotedblleft{}over\textquotedblright{} (MW; CDIAL 279): \textquotedblleft{}reading\textquotedblright{}, and then \textquotedblleft{}a lesson, a chapter\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a class, then the Sanskrit for a chapter.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{akṣara} is built from \emph{a-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{kṣara} \textquotedblleft{}perishing, melting away\textquotedblright{} (MW; CDIAL 38): \textquotedblleft{}imperishable\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}a syllable, a letter\textquotedblright{}. It lives on as Hindi \emph{ākhar} \textquotedblleft{}letter\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 38).

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{पदम्} (padam)}{पदम् (padam)}]{\sk{पदम्} (padam) — a word}

\label{lesson:SA-C168-padam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a syllable, then the Sanskrit for a colour.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{पदम्}}
\textbf{\sk{पदम्}} — \emph{padam} — \textquotedblleft{}a word\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pada} first meant \textquotedblleft{}a step, a footstep, a track\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7747), built on \emph{pad} \textquotedblleft{}foot\textquotedblright{}, and then a step of speech, \textquotedblleft{}a word\textquotedblright{}. It is inherited from Indo-European, cousin of Greek \emph{pedon} \textquotedblleft{}ground\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
